items.title: News Analysis: Military exercise highlights Europe's bid for role in Ukraine peace talks
text: WARSAW, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- As a new round of talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine approaches, the Britain- and France-led Coalition of the Willing launched its first military exercise in Poland on Monday to prepare for a possible deployment to Ukraine after hostilities end.
The exercise comes as European officials press for a role in the negotiations and analysts say the coalition is seeking to demonstrate its military credibility.

Russia, however, criticized such a deployment, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova warning Saturday that any foreign military units deployed in Ukraine would be regarded as legitimate targets.
The exercise, code-named "KOALICJA 26.2," runs from Nov. 9 to 22 and involves about 2,800 military personnel from 11 countries, including Britain, France, Germany, Belgium, Spain and Poland.

According to the British Ministry of Defence, the exercise will test command-and-control arrangements, rehearse the movement of personnel, equipment and supplies, and assess how different units can operate together as a multinational force.
"This isn't a hypothetical plan, it's a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops," British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a statement.

Directed from its operational headquarters in Paris, the multinational force has its land and air components around Nowa Deba in southeastern Poland, about 100 km from the Ukrainian border, while Turkish forces test arrangements for maritime mine clearance in Istanbul.
The drills are being held under the Coalition of the Willing, a group established in 2025 that comprises more than 30 countries, mostly European ones. The United States is not included.
Poland's Defense Ministry said the country hosts the main part of the exercise and provides logistical support, but did not plan to send troops to Ukraine after the conflict ends.
The exercise began a day before Russia, the United States and Ukraine were due to resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, amid disagreements over Europe's participation.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Monday that the European Union (EU) would be present while the Kremlin said the core negotiations would involve Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The exact format of European participation remained unclear.
Euronews reported Monday that concerns were growing in European capitals that decisions on the continent's security could be made without their involvement.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stressed Friday the bloc's role in Europe's security architecture and the need to integrate Ukraine into it. She said any peace agreement would require the EU's involvement to be implemented.
French daily Le Monde said the exercise was intended to demonstrate the coalition's military credibility, with European countries hoping it would give them a say in discussions on Ukraine's future.

items.title: Merz nominates Ilse Aigner for German presidency
text: BERLIN, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Monday nominated Ilse Aigner for the country's presidency, a move that could see Germany elect its first female head of state.
Merz, who also heads the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), announced the decision at a press conference in Berlin, confirming that the CDU's federal executive board had backed his proposal.
Aigner currently serves as president of the Bavarian state parliament and is a member of the Christian Social Union (CSU).
Amid geopolitical crises and rising extremism, Germany needs a president who can unite the country and provide guidance, Merz said.
Also at the press conference, Aigner said she aims to be a candidate of the "strong center" to bridge social divides and counter populist and extremist forces.

The next German federal president will be elected by the Federal Convention on Jan. 30 next year. The convention, consisting of members of the lower house of parliament and representatives from federal states, assembles only every five years to elect the federal president.
Given the solid majority held by supporting parties in the convention, Aigner is widely expected to win the election.  ■

items.title: Gift from Chinese hometown warms US elder's heart
text: In 1932, David Victor Plymire, then less than a year old, was carried by his parents from New York to Huangyuan County in northwest China's Qinghai Province. He spent the next 17 years there, growing up in the place he would always call home.
He came back in 1987. In the decades since, he has made more than 20 round trips across the Pacific, making the rounds in the United States to raise funds and purchase supplies for the county.
Those efforts have brought more than 30 pieces of medical equipment, worth a total of 6 million yuan (about $895,000), to Huangyuan County People's Hospital.

Today, at 95, Plymire still calls Huangyuan his hometown. Recently, a gift from the county arrived at his home in Missouri in the US. Half a world away, his bond with the land where he grew up has never broken.

items.title: Chinese medical team conducts health outreach in Sierra Leone
text: FREETOWN, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- An 11-member joint delegation of the 27th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone and an expert team from the Chinese Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has provided medical consultations and health screenings to about 250 residents of Sangbaia Community, northern Sierra Leone.

The three-day mission that ended over the weekend included infectious disease prevention lectures, first-responder emergency training and free medical outreach for Chinese and Sierra Leonean employees at Leone Rock Metal Group and residents of the surrounding communities.

On Friday, the Chinese medical team held sessions on Ebola prevention and malaria control at Leone Rock, alongside practical first-aid training that included demonstrations of cardiopulmonary resuscitation techniques for responding to cardiac emergencies.
A free multidisciplinary medical clinic followed, offering consultations, examinations and treatment.

The delegation provided medical services to Sangbaia Community on Saturday, where specialists conducted blood pressure and blood glucose checks, eye examinations, cataract screenings, traditional Chinese medicine treatment and free essential medicines.
Residents also received acupuncture and tuina massage therapy for muscle and joint-related complaints.

Leone Rock's community department manager Alusine Sesay welcomed the outreach, saying community development also requires investment in people's health. "We appreciate the medical team for making this initiative possible and for dedicating their time and expertise to serving the people of Sangbaia," Sesay said.
Ibrahim Keita, a local chief, expressed gratitude to the Chinese medical experts for bringing essential healthcare services closer to residents, particularly children.

items.title: Explainer: How the CIIE is reshaping global trade
text: SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- When U.S. essential oil producer doTERRA first attended the China International Import Expo (CIIE) in 2018, it arrived with a modest 9-square-meter booth and an experimental approach. To its surprise, it secured 380 million yuan (about 56 million U.S. dollars) in intended orders and buyer interest.

Eight years later, its exhibition space has grown to 300 square meters. Beyond the exhibition hall, the company now sources more essential oils from China than from any of the other 44 countries in its global supply network, while developing products based on Chinese plants for markets at home and abroad.

The company's trajectory reflects a broader change in the role of the CIIE. What began as a platform for overseas companies to display their products has increasingly become a place where they build lasting business ties, develop products with Chinese partners and connect with markets far beyond China.

For international businesses, the value of the expo is no longer measured only by the buyers they meet or the orders they secure. It is also found in the supply chains, research partnerships and commercial networks that take shape around it.
The CIIE's most visible contribution has been to help overseas products make the journey from exhibition booths to the Chinese market.

Over the first eight editions, more than 3,400 new products, technologies and services made their debuts at the expo, while cumulative intended deals exceeded 580 billion dollars, according to the organizer.

Continuing that momentum, the ninth edition has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors from 162 countries, regions and international organizations, with more than 480 products set to make their global, Asian or Chinese debuts, a record high. More than 2,000 exhibitors are participating for the first time.
For some companies, the expo has offered a first foothold in a market that might otherwise be difficult to enter.

Peruvian alpaca toy brand Warmpaca, for example, made its debut at the inaugural CIIE in 2018 also with a 9-square-meter booth. The response from Chinese consumers helped the family business expand its reach. It now sells its products in more than 30 shopping malls across China and through e-commerce platforms, with annual sales exceeding 30,000 units.
For companies still seeking to enter the Chinese market, the expo can also serve as a testing ground for consumer demand and a meeting point with potential local partners.

Swiss sun care brand Eiger, making its debut at this year's event, is looking to enter China as interest in outdoor activities, hiking and skin protection grows, said Simone Portmann, co-owner of the company.

Eiger has begun working with a local partner and plans to launch online sales in China in the coming weeks. Portmann said the company saw an opportunity among Chinese consumers increasingly interested in skincare and outdoor pursuits.

"It begins with the first step, and we are very confident," she said. "We felt that now is the right moment because the market is developing a lot. People are starting to care about their health; they care about doing outdoor sports, hiking, climbing and trail running."

items.title: China's foreign trade growth picks up pace in first 10 months
text: BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade in goods maintained strong growth momentum in the first 10 months of 2026, with imports posting especially robust gains, official data showed Tuesday.

Total imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year over the period, accelerating from 18.8 percent in the first nine months, according to the General Administration of Customs. Imports surged 23.6 percent, while exports rose 17.6 percent during the January-October period.

items.title: Fragrance become young Chinese's 'emotional companion'
text: Women try incense-making under the guidance of a staff member at an agarwood museum in Xianyou County, southeast China's Fujian Province, on Sept. 24, 2025. (Xinhua/Jiang Kehong)
Lighting incense before bed has become a nightly ritual for a woman surnamed Chen, a 28-year-old working in the internet industry.
"My brain switches to rest mode, and the house smells nice. I feel good," she said.
She is not alone. On social media, many users share their experiences with fragrance, which is increasingly becoming an "emotional companion" for young Chinese.

Dapu town in Yongchun county, Quanzhou city, southeast China's Fujian Province, is the birthplace of Yongchun incense and a major production hub for the industry. The craft dates back to the late Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and early Qing Dynasty (1644-1911). In 2021, Fujian incense-making craft, represented by Yongchun incense, was added to China's national intangible cultural heritage list.

The best-known type is bamboo incense. Lin Wenxi, a national-level inheritor of the craft, said it is made with local bamboo as the core, wrapped in natural plant materials that bind the powdered herbs. Craftspeople complete more than 10 steps by hand, producing a mild, lasting scent.

Yongchun incense has grown into an industry spanning the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors. The county has about 300 incense makers employing more than 30,000 people and producing over 1,000 varieties of products. The output value of the incense industrial chain has surpassed 10 billion yuan (about $1.5 billion). Yongchun incense products are sold in many countries and regions.

In the first five months of this year, the gross merchandise volume generated by livestream sales of Yongchun incense sticks and new Chinese-style aromatherapy products rose 461 percent year on year, with young consumers accounting for more than 60 percent of buyers.

One Dapu company uses artificial intelligence to analyze scent trends on e-commerce platforms, then refines the ingredient ratios in traditional formulas to develop fragrances and gift sets that appeal to young consumers.

Another local factory, which started as a family workshop in 1983, has grown into a business spanning research and development, manufacturing, cultural and creative product development, and tourism. Its incense-themed cultural and creative park was named one of Fujian's first sightseeing factories, where visitors can try their hand at making incense.

Local firms are also expanding beyond traditional incense products into portable incense, car and home fragrances, and cultural and creative souvenirs. These categories are gaining market share, while orders from stores, scenic spots and high-end hotels continue to rise.

In recent years, Yongchun has joined forces with Anxi, known for its tea, and Dehua, known for porcelain, to build a national demonstration zone for the integrated development of the tea, porcelain and incense industries.

White House briefly on lockdown after car crashes near Lafayette Park
text: Police officers investigate the scene where a car drove onto the sidewalk and struck an informational sign near Lafayette Park near the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Nov. 9, 2026. The White House was briefly placed on lockdown on Monday after two separate security incidents occurred near Lafayette Park, just north of the presidential residence. In one incident, a car drove onto the sidewalk and struck an informational sign, while in the other, an individual jumped a barricade near the park's northwest corner. (Xinhua/Li Rui)
WASHINGTON, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- The White House was briefly placed on lockdown on Monday after two separate security incidents occurred near Lafayette Park, just north of the presidential residence.
In one incident, a car drove onto the sidewalk and struck an informational sign, while in the other, an individual jumped a barricade near the park's northwest corner.

Video footage posted on social media showed a silver sedan driving onto the sidewalk just north of Lafayette Park, which is located directly north of the White House. The driver was seen struggling with Secret Service officers and National Guard personnel.

"The driver was combative with law enforcement but was quickly placed under arrest," the Secret Service said in a statement, as quoted by NBC Washington. "Around the same time, a second individual jumped a barricade near the northwest corner of Lafayette Park. That individual was also quickly placed under arrest."
The identities of the two individuals and their motives were not immediately clear.
The White House was placed under lockdown for about half an hour before normal operations resumed.

items.title: China pledges continued ecological conservation and climate action at COP31
text: China will continue to advance ecological conservation and take concrete action on climate change while working with other countries to strengthen global climate governance, Minister of Ecology and Environment Huang Runqiu said at a COP31 side event.
Officially known as the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, the UN gathering kicked off on Monday and will run through Nov 20.

Speaking at the China Pavilion event themed "ecological civilization and the practice of building a beautiful China", Huang said ecological civilization represents a historical trend and a new requirement for harmony between humanity and nature.
The minister listed a series of achievements China has made in promoting the construction of ecological civilization.

The country has completed ultra-low-emission upgrades for coal-fired power units totaling 1.17 billion kilowatts and crude steel production capacity totaling 1 billion metric tons, Huang said. Installed wind and solar capacity has exceeded 2 billion kW, which is roughly half of the global total, while photovoltaic power has surpassed coal-fired power to become the country's largest source of installed generating capacity.

Over the past five years, the average concentration of PM2.5 particulate matter fell by 20 percent and days with heavy air pollution declined by 25 percent, he said. The proportion of national surface-water sections with fairly good-quality water reached 91.4 percent.

China has a five-tier surface water quality system, with Grade I being the highest. Water rated Grade III or above is considered of fairly good quality and is suitable for the survival of most aquatic organisms.

Huang said China's forest coverage rate has reached 25.09 percent and forest stock has exceeded 20 billion cubic meters. Ninety percent of its terrestrial ecosystem types and 74 percent of populations of key nationally protected wildlife species are under effective protection.

The next five years will be crucial for building a Beautiful China and achieving carbon peaking, Huang said. China will coordinate carbon reduction, pollution control, ecological conservation and economic growth.
The country aims to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and realize carbon neutrality before 2060.

China will remain committed to concrete climate action, uphold multilateralism and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, and fully and effectively implement the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement, he said.

China stands ready to deepen cooperation with all parties, promote practical outcomes at COP31 and help build a more equitable, reasonable and mutually beneficial global climate governance system, Huang added.

items.title: Golden Rooster in Xiamen: from screen to streets
text: The 2026 China Golden Rooster & Hundred Flowers Film Festival opened in Xiamen, East China's Fujian province, on Nov 6, bringing filmmakers together to celebrate cinema and explore the city beyond the screen.

For filmmakers returning year after year, Xiamen offers more than scenic coastal views and local delicacies. Its warm hospitality also makes it a welcoming destination for film production and cultural exchange.
As 2,000 people gather to watch a film, one thing remains clear: even in the age of short videos, the magic of the big screen is worth holding on to.

items.title: Chinese envoy urges action on Ukraine peace talks
text: A Chinese envoy to the United Nations on Monday called on parties concerned to seize the opportunity for peace talks and work toward a political settlement of the Ukraine crisis, as Russia, Ukraine and the United States prepare for a new round of trilateral negotiations.

"The Ukraine issue is approaching a critical moment for a negotiated settlement, and the international community's calls for peace and its encouragement of peace talks are growing ever stronger," Sun Lei, China's deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, told a UN Security Council meeting on Ukraine.

Sun said recent engagements among key stakeholders have sent positive signals, adding that China supports efforts conducive to peace and hopes the parties will maintain the positive momentum toward an early political settlement.
"We must strengthen the will for peace and seize the window of opportunity for peace talks," Sun said.

He noted that the parties have recently expressed their views on achieving a political settlement, while the international community has undertaken extensive diplomatic efforts to promote negotiations.

"The parties concerned should demonstrate political will, maintain contact and communication, build consensus step by step, and work together toward a comprehensive, durable and binding peace agreement," he said.
Sun's remarks came ahead of a new round of trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States, scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates.
Ukraine's negotiating delegation departed for Abu Dhabi on Monday, according to Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, Xinhua reported.

Representatives from the UK, France, Germany and Italy, along with officials from NATO and the European Commission, also are expected to be present in Abu Dhabi, where Ukraine plans to hold separate coordination meetings with European partners, Umerov said.
The negotiations will mark the first trilateral meeting involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States since February.

On the humanitarian situation, Sun called for efforts to de-escalate tensions and protect civilians, noting recent prisoner exchanges and a localized humanitarian ceasefire that allowed civilians to evacuate frontline areas and receive assistance.

"We call on the parties to put people's lives first, exercise calm and restraint, and effectively protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, especially women, children and other victims of the conflict," he said.
Sun also urged intensified humanitarian relief efforts and called on the parties to ensure proper treatment of prisoners of war and detained persons in accordance with applicable international law.
Addressing the prospects for lasting peace, Sun stressed the need to tackle the underlying causes of the crisis.
"There are no winners in conflict and war," he said.

items.title: Highland grapes transform barren plateau into thriving base
text: In autumn, rows of grapevines stretch as far as the eye can see across the Yarlung Zangbo River valley in the Xizang autonomous region, a striking scene against the plateau landscape.
This picturesque scenery can be seen at the Tharmo village in Sangri county, Lhokha city, where land once considered difficult to cultivate has been turned into a thriving grape-growing area.
The transformation began in 2011, when a 1-hectare trial plot was established in Tharmo to test whether grapes could grow in a high-altitude environment.
Today, vineyards across Tharmo and surrounding villages in Sangri cover about 667 hectares.
However, the journey has not been without challenges.

At that time, the area, located at an altitude of around 3,600 meters, was considered too harsh an environment for grape cultivation, with strong winds, sandy and saline-alkali soil, frost and hail posing major challenges to cultivation efforts.

"The biggest challenge was the high altitude, because no one had tried growing grapes at this elevation before," said Li Xiaoping, deputy general manager of Pazhu Vineyard, a major company involved in the Sangri grape industry.

Over the years, the company worked with research institutions to develop cultivation methods adapted to the plateau environment, including soil improvement, irrigation systems and ecological restoration measures. The process progressed from initial experiments to pilot-scale trials, and eventually large-scale planting.

The efforts gradually paid off. "After eight years of testing more than 60 varieties, we selected six that were suitable for the high-altitude environment of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the Yarlung Zangbo River valley," Li said. The region's strong ultraviolet radiation, dry climate and significant day-night temperature differences are believed to contribute to distinct grape characteristics.

One selected variety is Yajiang No 1, a grape variety specifically developed for the plateau environment. With red skin, red flesh and a red core, it is more tolerant to the cold plateau environment and is mainly used to produce dry reds and some sweet wines, he said.

Studies by the Institute of Botany of the Chinese Academy of Sciences found that anthocyanin levels in the grapes could be six to 12 times higher than those in grapes from plain regions, according to Science and Technology Daily.
The highland grapes were later processed into wine products. Pazhu Vineyard began commercial wine production in 2021 and now produces 10 varieties of wine.

In 2025, the winery produced about 500,000 bottles, with output continuing to increase. Its products are sold to several domestic markets and exported to Hong Kong, while the company continues to explore overseas markets, Li said.
Beyond wine production, the grape industry also brought job opportunities to local residents who can earn income without leaving their communities.

Sonam Penpa, a local employee at Pazhu Vineyard, previously worked in construction far from his hometown. "Before the vineyard was built, we had to leave home to find work elsewhere," he said. "After the vineyard was established, we could work close to home all year round and have a stable income."

items.title: China's tariff move seen as stability boost
text: China's decision to extend the suspension of additional tariffs on goods from the United States is seen to be conducive to stabilizing bilateral trade ties, improving business confidence and providing greater predictability for companies navigating an uncertain global economic environment, analysts and business executives said.

The Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council has announced that China will extend the suspension of an additional 24 percent tariff on US imports for two months, starting on Tuesday afternoon, while maintaining a 10 percent additional tariff.

At the same time, the commission said China has noted repeated US statements about plans to replace tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which were struck down by the US Supreme Court, with tariffs under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974. China will closely monitor subsequent US measures and adjust its tariff countermeasures accordingly, it added.

Furthermore, the Ministry of Commerce announced on Monday that China will extend by another two months, starting on Tuesday, the suspension of measures against 11 US entities placed on its unreliable entity list in April 2025. Export restrictions on dual-use items involving 16 other US entities will remain suspended for two more months.

Chinese companies seeking to conduct business with the 11 entities can apply for approval, while exporters seeking to supply dual-use items to the 16 entities must obtain licenses from the ministry. Applications meeting regulatory requirements will be approved, said a ministry spokesperson.

Fu Suixin, an associate researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of American Studies, said greater tariff and trade policy stability would allow businesses on both sides to make investment and sourcing decisions with more confidence, amid global supply chain adjustments, volatile energy costs and changing trade policies.

Zhao Minghao, a professor and deputy director of Fudan University's Center for American Studies in Shanghai, said amid persistent differences over trade and technology, sustained high-level dialogue and effective communication mechanisms could help China and the US manage disputes and maintain more predictable economic ties.

Despite persistent trade tensions, China-US trade in goods grew 4.1 percent year-on-year to 3.18 trillion yuan ($476.5 billion) in the first three quarters of 2026, data from the General Administration of Customs showed.

Wang Ruibin, chairman of Ningbo Sibranch Microelectronics Technology Co, a semiconductor silicon wafer processor based in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, said the duty adjustments and reciprocal tariff reductions can provide greater pricing certainty for businesses in both China and the US.
The company imported nearly 4 million yuan worth of silicon wafers in the first 10 months of 2026, up 30 percent year-on-year, according to Ningbo Customs.
"US-made products account for nearly 60 percent of our silicon wafer imports, and our finished products are mainly exported to the US, Vietnam and Malaysia," Wang said.
For US companies operating in China, bilateral economic ties extend well beyond tariffs.

items.title: China aims to close healthcare gap with digital tech
text: Digital technologies are opening up new possibilities for making medical services more accessible, from artificial intelligence-assisted clinical applications to efforts to bring specialist expertise to primary-level healthcare institutions.

Turning these possibilities into practical services for communities was a key topic at a smart healthcare roundtable held in Beijing in early November, bringing together Chinese and overseas medical professionals, healthcare businesses and institution representatives.
The roundtable was a thematic event of the 15th China Overseas Investment Fair, hosted by the China Overseas Development Association.

Representatives from the League of Arab States, Turkiye, Pakistan, Russia, Iraq, Brazil, Cuba, Namibia, and the Comoros shared their countries' healthcare priorities, including gaps in primary-level services and demand for digital healthcare. Many expressed interest in cooperating with Chinese partners on smart healthcare and medical industry investment.

In the meeting, hospital administrators and clinical experts discussed how digital technologies could support hospital operations and the development of medical specialties. Topics included group-based hospital management, national regional medical centers, and applications ranging from AI-assisted cardiovascular diagnosis and treatment to rehabilitation based on traditional Chinese medicine, wound repair, and childhood scar prevention and treatment.
Participants also discussed the challenges of expanding AI applications in healthcare.

Another discussion focus was extending professional medical support to grassroots communities. The Beijing Injury Repair Association introduced its Healthy Journey Along the Long March public welfare project, which plans to organize multidisciplinary medical specialists to provide free consultations and assistance in primary-level communities.

Coinciding with the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March (1934-36), the initiative will use a smart healthcare information platform to support technology deployment, academic exchanges and professional training.

Pharmaceutical and medical device companies also presented developments in clinical nutrition, anti-infective wound care, cardiovascular devices, chronic disease testing, and women's reproductive health, sharing examples of domestic innovations entering practical applications and overseas markets.

Participants discussed how clinical needs, technological innovation and overseas market demand could be better connected, with digital technologies driving stronger primary healthcare and international cooperation.

items.title: Weak domestic demand blunts top sales period
text:
By CAO YINGYING | 
          China Daily |
          Updated: 2026-11-09 09:24

China's traditionally robust auto sales season of "Golden September and Silver October" lost much of its shine this year. However, surging overseas shipments are acting as a buffer against the shrinking domestic market.

The China Passenger Car Association estimates retail sales of passenger vehicles in China dropped to 1.6 million units in October, down 28.9 percent year-on-year. Full-year domestic passenger vehicle retail sales are estimated at 18.5 million units, down 22.1 percent from 23.74 million in 2025.
Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the CPCA, attributed the worse-than-expected slump to the expiry of purchase-tax incentives for new energy vehicles and geopolitical conflicts pushing up oil prices.
He added that conditions may improve in 2027 as inventory pressures ease and new vehicle supply cycles recover, setting the car market on course for a recovery.

The China Automobile Dealers Association noted that national holiday promotions and autumn auto shows lifted showroom traffic and orders in early October, but momentum faded in the second half of the month. A wait-and-see sentiment persisted, with consumers holding out for year-end discounts, stretching decision-making cycles and intensifying price competition.
"The 'Golden September, Silver October' phenomenon has basically vanished for the first time and may become a thing of the past," said Gui Shengyue, vice-chairman of the board of Geely Auto.

The weak season indicates a market shift in which cars are no longer basic transportation tools and consumers no longer buy cars purely as durable necessities, placing more value on technology and other attributes. Most orders are from trade-ins and second purchases, with increased consumer hesitation.
Overseas markets, once merely a growth supplement, have now become a pillar for stabilizing overall sales and offsetting weakening domestic demand.

In terms of different brands, BYD remained the top seller in October with 490,200 units delivered, up 10.97 percent year-on-year and 5.74 percent month-on-month. But the headline growth masks weakness at home: BYD's domestic retail volumes have fallen every month so far in 2026.

From July to October, its domestic sales dropped 9.18 percent, 14.34 percent, 12.97 percent and 10.57 percent year-on-year, respectively. The automaker's overall positive growth was largely propped up by overseas deliveries.

SAIC Motor ranked second with around 430,000 units, down 5.28 percent year-on-year. Geely's October sales stood at 310,000 units, eking out 1 percent annual growth. Chery followed with 295,900 units, up 5.3 percent year-on-year.

Great Wall Motor, by contrast, delivered 120,300 units, a 15.87 percent drop. Changan Auto reported October sales of 233,200 units, down 16.23 percent year-on-year even as its overseas deliveries jumped 77.3 percent year-on-year to 102,500 units.
New energy brands showed mixed results, with overseas expansion delivering outsized gains for some.

More than 480 exhibits made global, Asian or Chinese debuts. Qualcomm brought a 6G terminal prototype out of the lab. Medtronic’s China-developed Kanghui orthopedic surgical robot had its world premiere. And a rare type of durian tree fruit, the Malaysian white durian, made its global debut.

items.title: From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019240/From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
text: The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) closed in Shanghai on Tuesday after showcasing cutting-edge technologies in artificial intelligence, commercial aerospace, and innovative drugs.

The six-day event drew exhibitors from a record 162 countries, regions, and international organizations. A total of 4,142 overseas companies took part — also a record high — with more than 480 representative products making their global, Asian, or China debut.

U.S. wireless chipmaker Qualcomm exhibited the world’s first 6G terminal prototype — the first time the device has been shown publicly outside the lab. The prototype has been used in joint tests with China Mobile, China’s largest telecom operator, and Chinese telecom equipment manufacturer ZTE. The prototype will provide the foundation for 6G chips and support the technology’s commercial rollout.

The event featured an expanded medical devices and health care exhibition area, acting as the stage for the China debut of pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca’s new hypertension medication baxdrostat. The oral medication works by inhibiting the enzyme aldosterone synthase, which helps synthesize the blood pressure-regulating hormone aldosterone, and was approved in the U.S. in May.

German optical giant Zeiss also made its global debut of its new non-spherical lens PT Lunana, designed for myopia correction. Novartis, a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical company, showcased ianalumab, a drug used for treating the autoimmune illness Sjögren’s disease — also a China debut.

American electric vehicle company Tesla presented its Cybercab autonomous vehicle. Lacking a steering wheel or pedals, the vehicle relies on cameras and AI to drive. Hexagon — a global digital reality and metrology tech company — also displayed its industrial humanoid robot AEON.

Aerospace technology was also present, including the Zhuque-3 rocket developed by Chinese commercial aerospace company LandSpace. The rocket’s reusable booster, which uses liquid oxygen and methane as fuel, can land vertically, first achieved by the company in August.

Beyond showcasing new tech, the expo held its first exhibition area for 100 long-established, reputable international brands — from Canadian shoe companies to Spanish wineries — as well as hosted a trade and investment “matchmaking” conference, where companies and buyers met to sign cooperation agreements. The latter conference attracted more than 600 exhibitors and over 2,000 buyers from 59 countries and regions.
The deals reached at this year’s expo are projected to be worth a total of $85.45 billion over the coming year, up 2.3% from last year and a record high.

items.title: Postscript: China Opens School Dedicated to Ancient Chinese Writing
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019239/Postscript: China Opens School Dedicated to Ancient Chinese Writing
text: China has opened its first school dedicated to declining and obscure fields of study, with a focus on ancient and classical Chinese texts.

The School for Rare and Endangered Disciplines was inaugurated in Beijing on Nov. 6 under the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (UCASS). At the opening, the university also announced the launch of a national alliance of more than 80 universities, museums, and cultural and research institutions to share resources, conduct collaborative research, and cultivate talent in related fields.

The school comes as the number of scholars studying ancient Chinese scripts dwindles. Nationwide, only about 500 people work in ancient Chinese writing studies, and of the roughly 4,500 known oracle bone characters — the oldest known fully developed form of Chinese writing and widely used for divination purposes during the Shang dynasty (c.1600–1046 BC) — nearly two-thirds remain undeciphered, underlining the need for further research.

The initiative also builds on previous attempts by UCASS to preserve such fields, such as establishing an institute for rare and endangered studies in 2024 to train future talent in fields such as bamboo and silk studies, which examines script on the two materials, as well as classical studies, Turkic studies, and Assyriology, or studies of the Ancient Near East.

Each student of the new school’s bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degree courses will be mentored by two members of the school’s more than 140 faculty members. UCASS has also built dedicated laboratories for the school’s use.

Students may pursue research in oracle bone studies, bamboo and silk studies, and classical studies. They may also train in over 10 ancient ethnic scripts, including Turkic, Tangut, Khitan, Jurchen, Manchu, Old Tibetan, Old Yi, Phags-pa, Naxi Dongba, and Zhuang.

“Ancient scripts like oracle bone script are on the verge of being lost, and some frontier history research relies on the survival of the country’s cultural roots and its long-term development,” Huang Dekuan, director of the Research and Conservation Center for Unearthed Texts at Tsinghua University, told state broadcaster CCTV.
Such disciplines are also hampered by scattered resources and research institutions working in isolation — key obstacles to research and transmission, according to CCTV.

China has called for increased focus on cultural heritage preservation in recent years. At an October press conference on cultural heritage protection, government officials called for advancing cultural heritage as a discipline, cultivating interdisciplinary talent in the field, and encouraging qualified universities to establish cultural heritage schools.

In a Nov. 7 commentary, domestic media outlet The Beijing News wrote that by emphasizing rare and endangered disciplines, the new school offers a lesson to other universities: schools should develop their own distinctive majors, resist the urge to offer only popular fields, and actively strengthen less mainstream majors.
“Only then can a university truly serve education,” it stated.

items.title: Fallback to First Choice: Why Chinese Parents Are Rethinking Vocational Schools
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019245/Fallback to First Choice: Why Chinese Parents Are Rethinking Vocational Schools
text: Coming from a Shanghai family with a strong academic background, Yang Fan had always felt studying at university was his destiny. The only problem was, he was flunking middle school.

“He’d make the same mistake with a character the entire semester. I just couldn’t get him to do it right,” says his mother, Zhao Xuan, who could only look on in frustration as Yang struggled with his homework night after night. “Given how much it was taking for him to get through middle school, I felt high school would crush him.”

Last summer, with the conventional academic pathway looking a bad fit for their 15-year-old son, Zhao and her husband began to consider China’s integrated secondary vocational-to-undergraduate articulation program. Launched as a 2014 pilot in Shanghai, the initiative sees students spend up to three years at a vocational school before transitioning to a partner university to complete a related four-year bachelor’s degree program.
Over the past 12 years, the number of participating educational institutions has rapidly expanded, now covering at least seven provincial regions, and applications have soared.

Shanghai alone has established 91 majors across 38 vocational schools and 18 universities, enrolling about 20,000 students and producing six cohorts of graduates. Planned enrollment this year was 2,756, up from just 120 in 2014 and a 17.5% increase from 2025.

Programs cover diverse fields including robotics, accounting, digital media arts, big data engineering, logistics, environmental design, hospitality management, cultural heritage restoration, smart manufacturing, performing arts, sound recording, information security, and materials science.

The trend reflects a sea change in attitudes toward vocational education in China. Technical skills training has long been stigmatized as “low status” and a “fallback option,” but as the country’s workforce undergoes a massive restructuring driven by an aging population, advancements in artificial intelligence, and an economic slowdown, more people feel it now makes students more employable compared to those with purely academic backgrounds.

In real terms, most students in the integrated program say their experiences are far less stressful than those of their peers at traditional Chinese high schools, and that they are encouraged to focus more on their personal strengths rather than sticking to a one-size-fits-all curriculum.

However, because most applicants are only in their mid-teens, it’s often parents who make the final decision, with research suggesting that more-passive children have only a vague idea of, or interest in, what might lie ahead.

It was only when Zhao learned that the prestigious Shanghai Maritime University (SMU) would join the integrated secondary vocational-to-undergraduate articulation program in 2026 that she was sure the pathway was a “realistic match” for Yang.

items.title: More Chinese Regions to Require Autumn and Spring School Breaks
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019236/More Chinese Regions to Require Autumn and Spring School Breaks
text: More Chinese regions are implementing autumn and spring breaks in compulsory education, expanding a decadelong national initiative. Some have also waived fees for students on break and rolled out support measures to help parents take leave at the same time as their children.

Spring and autumn holidays across all compulsory education schools have been rolled out provincewide in at least 15 provinces, as well as numerous cities in other provinces, such as the southern megacity of Shenzhen, domestic media reported last week. In China, compulsory education lasts nine years, encompassing primary and middle school. Breaks will occur in November and April for four to five days each.

The reform dates back to 2004, when Hangzhou, capital of the eastern province of Zhejiang, piloted the breaks. In 2013, the initiative expanded nationally when the State Council issued an announcement encouraging local governments to adopt it, and the rollout accelerated again in 2025 when central authorities urged more schools to implement the holidays.
Chu Zhaohui, a researcher at the China National Academy of Educational Sciences, told domestic media outlet Red Star News that the holidays actually boost learning.
“Learning isn’t confined to schools or taught only by teachers and parents,” Chu said, adding that the holidays give students space for self-exploration.

At the same time as introducing spring and autumn holiday policies, many cities have also added supporting measures so parents can sync their leave. In October, Longnan city in the northwestern Gansu province encouraged employers to implement paid leave and prioritize compensatory rest for employees with school-age children, aligning staff leave with school holidays.

Foshan, a city in the southern Guangdong province, also issued a proposal on Nov. 3 calling on employers to prioritize arranging leave for employees with children during the autumn holiday. The city’s five-day autumn break begins Nov. 11.

Many tourist spots are also waiving entrance fees for children during the upcoming fall break. In the eastern city of Wuxi, a theme park dropped entry fees for students 16 and under throughout November; 15 top tourism sites in Huangshan in the eastern Anhui province, a city known for its mountain of the same name, are now entry-free for children under 18; and the Dujiangyan scenic area in the southwestern Sichuan province waived fees for primary and middle school students between Nov. 12 and 16.

The breaks have significantly boosted travel demand, according to online travel booking platform Qunar. Data from Qunar revealed that in November, air ticket bookings for children 12 and under increased 1.6 times year on year, while parent bookings rose by 50%.

Wang Qiyan, director of the Leisure Economy Research Center at Renmin University, told Red Star News that spring and autumn breaks “enable off-peak travel, avoiding the packed scenic spots of winter and summer vacations.
(Header image: Tourists take photos of St. Sophia Square during the autumn break in Harbin, Heilongjiang province, Nov. 4, 2026. VCG)

items.title: A Bad Review, a Suicide, and a Debate Over Cyberbullying in China
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019228/A Bad Review, a Suicide, and a Debate Over Cyberbullying in China
text: On Oct. 6, 2026, a female customer posted complaints on multiple social media platforms about a fried skewer stall in Gao County, Yibin, in southwestern China’s Sichuan province. “Avoid XX Copper Pot Potatoes. The owner can’t take the heat,” she wrote. She had bought a 10-yuan ($1.40) fried food combo from the stall, run by a 33-year-old woman surnamed Hu, but was dissatisfied with the portion of potatoes. “She just refused to add potatoes afterward,” the customer added. Her location-tagged posts quickly spread, and negative comments about Hu and her stall flooded the comment sections.
Hu responded to the criticism, writing, “I stand behind my portions.” Three days later, on Oct. 9, she jumped into a river and died by suicide.

Hu had run the stall for more than four years, sleeping less than six hours a night. In her suicide note, she described the enormous pressures she faced in life. She had hoped to watch her child grow up, she wrote, but the video telling people to avoid her stall had been the straw that broke the camel’s back.

She also wrote: “These past two days I have experienced what I consider cyberbullying. One person complained about no potatoes in her order, and then the comments came flooding in about bad service and poor-tasting food.”

This was not the first tragedy of its kind. In August 2025, a 57-year-old obstetrician-gynecologist surnamed Shao in Zhoukou, central China’s Henan province, jumped to her death. According to her family, she had endured more than seven months of cyberbullying over a medical dispute. In 2023, after a primary school student in Wuhan, capital of the central Hubei province, was killed in a traffic accident on campus, his mother was subjected to online attacks and later jumped to her death. In cases like these, public opinion often attributes the tragedies to cyberbullying.
But in Hu’s case, labeling the entire incident “cyberbullying” and placing the blame on the customer who posted the negative review would exaggerate the power of a single act of expression.

The customer maintained that she was simply describing a genuine experience, with “no malice, incitement, or falsehood.” She did not insult or personally attack anyone, disclose private information, or call for coordinated attacks online or offline. Her criticism may have been harsh, subjective, or exaggerated, but based on the content of her posts alone, it is difficult to characterize it as cyberbullying.

Many negative comments about the stall owner appeared beneath the posts, but there is currently no evidence that they were all malicious. Public criticism can be harsh, but legal liability must rest on provable facts.

In July 2026, China released a draft Anti-Online Violence Law for public comment. It defines online violence as “concentrated or sustained” acts involving “insult and abuse, rumor-mongering and defamation, incitement of hatred,” and similar behavior. A negative review based on a genuine transaction cannot automatically be classified as cyberbullying because it has harmful consequences. Moreover, the draft has not yet become law.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: China's NEV exports surge 144.7% in Oct, growth expected to moderate as overseas markets mature
text: China's new-energy vehicle (NEV) exports surged 144.7 percent year-on-year in October, industry data showed on Monday, underscoring strong overseas demand even as domestic sales weakened. Industry analysts said that exports are likely to maintain robust momentum in the near term, although growth is likely to moderate as overseas markets mature and competition intensifies.

Chinese producers exported 582,000 passenger NEVs in October, up 3.9 percent from September, according to data released by the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA). Meanwhile, domestic NEV retail sales fell 13.7 percent year-on-year to 1.109 million units, although they rose 2.3 percent month-on-month.
Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the CPCA, told the Global Times on Monday that China's automobile exports are expected to shift from rapid growth this year to a more moderate pace in 2027.

Cui forecast that overall vehicle export growth could slow to about 10 percent next year as shipments to Russia stabilize and exports to the EU face mounting pressure. The Middle East region could provide additional growth, although prospects remain uncertain, he said.
Passenger NEV exports reached 4.472 million units in the first 10 months of 2026, up 139.7 percent year-on-year, according to the CPCA.

These figures also point to a changing export structure. NEVs accounted for 62.8 percent of China's passenger vehicle exports in October, up 20 percentage points from a year earlier. Battery electric vehicles represented 61.7 percent of NEV shipments, while conventional plug-in hybrids accounted for 33.7 percent.

Leading Chinese automakers recorded substantial overseas shipments. BYD exported 165,194 passenger NEVs in October, followed by Chery with 83,843 and Geely with 80,119, CPCA figures showed. Tesla China's exports reached 59,012 units.

Zhang Xiang, a researcher at the Automotive Industry Innovation Research Center of North China University of Technology, told the Global Times on Monday that Chinese automakers have established a competitive edge in the global NEV market through technological advances, mature supply chains and increasingly competitive products.

He said that he expects overseas demand to remain strong in the coming months, supporting continued export growth. However, as NEV adoption expands and initial demand is gradually absorbed, export growth is likely to return to a more sustainable pace over the longer term.

The expansion comes amid a changing international trade environment. The EU has imposed additional countervailing duties on China-made battery electric vehicles, while Chinese manufacturers are increasingly exploring emerging markets to diversify their overseas sales.

According to the International Energy Agency, sales of Chinese-made electric cars last year grew by 130 percent in Southeast Asia, 60 percent in the Middle East and 55 percent in Latin America, highlighting growing demand beyond traditional markets.

items.title: Buoyed by zero tariffs, African exporters eye bigger China market
text: Eight years after showcasing Kenyan avocados at the China International Import Expo (CIIE), Tiku Shah is back in Shanghai with a bigger ambition: doubling his company's avocado shipments to China next year.
For Shah, managing director of Kenyan avocado exporter Sunripe, China's latest tariff cuts have given his expansion plans a boost.
On May 1, China extended zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it maintains diplomatic ties, benefiting another 20 countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa.

Six months into the expansion, the CIIE, the world's largest import-themed expo and now in its ninth edition, offers a glimpse of how African exporters are seeking to turn lower trade costs into bigger orders, new partnerships, and opportunities to expand production at home.

Since fresh Kenyan avocados gained access to China in 2022, Sunripe has steadily developed its export business. The company has shipped some 500 to 600 tonnes to China so far this year, and Shah sees the elimination of tariffs as a chance to reach more Chinese consumers.
"It makes our products cheaper and more affordable, so more Chinese people can enjoy them," he said.
Beyond lower tariffs, Shah cited shipping and customs clearance as advantages. He said shipments from Kenya take about 25 days to reach China by sea and can clear customs within the day of arrival.

Chinese fruit importer Joy Wing Mau has also seen tangible benefits. Huang Li, the company's head of brand communications for the Chinese market, said tariffs on South African citrus had fallen from 10 to 12 percent to zero since May, reducing import costs by about 10 percent.

Since the policy took effect, the company's imports of South African citrus have risen 50 percent year on year. "The policy has encouraged more businesses to explore the Chinese market and generated more purchase orders," Huang said.
Alongside tariff cuts, China has upgraded its "green channel" for African agricultural and food products, streamlining quarantine procedures to facilitate imports.
At this year's CIIE, many first-time African exhibitors are seeking to capitalize on China's expanded zero-tariff policy and gain a foothold in the Chinese market.

Cote d'Ivoire's official delegation is making its debut in the CIIE's business exhibition this year, bringing more than 20 companies to a roughly 200-square-meter booth showcasing cocoa, cashews and tropical fruits.

"Many of our companies are testing the Chinese market for the first time, and their expectations are high," said Kaladji Fadiga, director general of the Cote d'Ivoire Export Agency. He said the agency has established a joint working group with the Chinese embassy to help exporters tap opportunities under the zero-tariff policy and connect with potential buyers at the CIIE.

This year's CIIE features an upgraded Asia-Africa products zone, with free exhibition space for the least-developed countries increased by 17 percent, giving more businesses a chance to showcase their products and connect with Chinese buyers.

items.title: Singapore Business Federation leads 54 firms to CIIE to unlock bilateral and regional opportunities
text: Singapore firms continue to value China as an important market, and the Southeast Asian country's extensive business networks and familiarity with Southeast Asian markets make it a valuable partner for Chinese enterprises looking to expand their regional footprint, an executive of the Singapore Business Federation said.

China remains a significant market for Singapore businesses, underpinned by its vast consumer market, evolving demand and focus on high-quality development, Mark Lee, chairman of SBF, said during an exclusive interview on the sidelines of the ongoing 9th China International Import Expo held in Shanghai on Friday.

The federation is leading a delegation of 54 Singapore firms to the CIIE. Since the inaugural CIIE in 2018, Singapore businesses have generated about 2.79 billion yuan ($420 million) in cumulative trade value through the event.

Spanning established household names and emerging businesses, participating Singaporean firms at the expo highlight the country's competitive strength in food, health and wellness, consumer innovation, financial services and professional solutions.

They include See Hai Tat Medical Hall (Singapore) Pte Ltd, which looks to grow its consumer presence in China, and Prima Food Pte Ltd, which wants to use the CIIE to explore opportunities in the Chinese market.

With Singapore set to be the ASEAN chair in 2027, the SBF's participation in the CIIE this year — as it has done across all previous editions of the expo — further highlights its role as a strategic bridge for Chinese enterprises looking to expand into the ASEAN market, Lee said.

"Singapore features transparent, trusted legal frameworks and strong intellectual property protection, which helps safeguard technology rights as solutions expand into ASEAN and other regions. We are also a financing hub," Lee said, adding that this explains why many of the country's professional services partners are at the CIIE. They include banks, advisory firms, human resources consultants, legal service providers and trade compliance specialists.

He highlighted that China is among the global leaders in AI and digitization. Singaporean businesses want to work closely and conduct business with their Chinese counterparts, and such collaborations are already underway.

Lee raised the example of Pony.ai, a Chinese autonomous vehicle AI company, which partnered with ComfortDelGro, a Singaporean transport operator that runs taxi and fleet services. They launched a robotaxi pilot in China's Guangzhou, Guangdong province, and following the pilot, a robotaxi service was rolled out earlier this year in a designated area in Singapore, using Pony.ai's technology.

"ComfortDelGro stated that the pilot supports its broader global strategy covering China and Singapore, since it provides fleet management services across multiple markets. This illustrates a strong model: proven Chinese technology, localized by Singapore companies, with plans to scale into other regions and countries," Lee said.
Singapore and China share longstanding economic ties, with bilateral trade in goods reaching approximately 895.9 billion yuan last year

items.title: Austrian chocolate maker Zotter sees sweet opportunities at CIIE
text: This undated file photo shows an aerial view of Zotter's chocolate theater in Bergl, Austria. Austrian chocolate maker Zotter has a chocolate theater in east China's Shanghai, which is almost the same as Zotter's chocolate theater in Bergl, Austria. Both theaters offer visitors chocolate tastings, hands-on chocolate-making experiences, film screenings and exhibitions.

items.title: Record number of product debuts at CIIE highlights China’s emerging role as innovation hub
text: "Show China your best." That is the invitation the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) extends to the world. The response? More than 480 products and technologies making their global, Asian or China debuts, from 6G device prototypes and AI computing systems to innovative medicines, luxury skincare and fragrances - a vibrant showcase of global innovation meeting the energy of China's vast consumer market that is more open to new products and ideas.

For global companies, the CIIE is more than a showcase for new products. It is a window into China - one that opens onto a vast consumer market, an evolving innovation landscape and expanding opportunities for international cooperation. What comes through that window is not just a flow of goods, but a deeper exchange of ideas, technologies and opportunities.

At Qualcomm's booth in the Technology and Equipment Exhibition Area, visitors are lining up to see what the US chipmaker describes as the world's first 6G device prototype compliant with the latest 3GPP specifications. Making its global debut at the expo, the prototype is among the booth's main attractions.

Another new arrival is the large-model-native agent phone STEPX Neo, which integrates applications and services including Alipay, Jianying (CapCut) and Trip.com. Its combination of hardware, software and AI models points to how AI agents could become more closely integrated into everyday mobile services.

Intel is taking a different approach to the AI boom, focusing on where computing power is generated and how it is supplied. Its CIIE debut is a computing solution that places computing clusters inside shipping containers, with flexible energy storage modules, allowing them to operate closer to renewable energy sources.

"Rather than bringing electricity to computing centers, it makes more sense to move computing clusters closer to where the electricity is generated," Intel China Chairman Wang Zhicong told the Global Times.
The solution, first conceived as an idea at last year's expo, combines computing power, renewable energy and storage, with Chinese energy and IT companies involved in its development.

The exhibits are not confined to technology and equipment. In healthcare, Roche is presenting nearly 100 debut and first-show exhibits, including innovative medicines for breast cancer, lupus nephritis and other diseases. Boehringer Ingelheim is showcasing 14 innovative pipeline products and solutions in human pharmaceuticals and animal health, with three therapies at the forefront of global R&D making their China debut.

Both companies are also looking to deepen their engagement with China's medical innovation ecosystem. Vivian Bian, CEO of Roche Pharma China, told the Global Times that Roche will take the CIIE as an important fulcrum for open cooperation, continue to increase its local investment, and deeply integrate into China's medical innovation ecosystem.

items.title: Annual CIIE opens in Shanghai, showcasing China's commitment to opening up
text: On Thursday morning, in the waiting lounge of the opening ceremony of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, two hours before the ceremony began, the guests had already begun arriving.

They took selfies, chatted, posed for group photos with old friends and gave interviews to the media. According to on-site observations by the Global Times, in the relaxing atmosphere, the words they mentioned most were "opportunity", "openness" and "market."

Running from Thursday to Tuesday next week, this year's CIIE has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors, with total exhibition area exceeding 440,000 square meters. Over 480 exhibits are set to make their global, Asian or China debut at the event, the highest number in history. In addition, nearly 200 companies and institutions have been "full attendees" at the CIIE for all nine editions.

In his keynote speech at the opening ceremony, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, said that the CIIE has witnessed China's firm determination and concrete actions to promote high-standard opening-up, the remarkable results and tremendous gains of businesses and people from various countries in sharing opportunities in the Chinese market, and the unremitting efforts and important contributions of visionary people from all walks of life in improving global economic governance, according to Xinhua News Agency.

This fully demonstrates China's strategic resolve in advancing high-standard opening-up, injecting valuable certainty, stability and confidence in development into the world, Hu Qimu, professor at the Maritime Silk Road Institute of Huaqiao University, told the Global Times on Thursday.

Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker of Austria, and UN Development Programme Administrator Alexander De Croo attended the opening ceremony and delivered remarks, Xinhua reported.

Ding's speech was welcomed by many executives from global multinational companies, who said they draw great inspiration from the speech and remain confident in honoring their long-term commitment to China.

Rogier Janssens, President of Merck China, told the Global Times that CIIE brings the world to China, and gives China a stronger voice in the global conversation. "As China moves into its 15th Five-Year Plan, the Expo's role is even more important," Janssens said.

The CIIE opening ceremony underscored the importance of openness, collaboration and innovation-driven development, further reinforcing Henkel's confidence in the long-term growth of the Chinese market, Anna An, President of Henkel China told the Global Times on Thursday.

Vice Premier Ding's speech reaffirmed China's steadfast commitment to high-standard opening-up and highlighted the country's important role in driving growth and building an open global economy, echoed Poh-Yian Koh, President of FedEx China.

items.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged spy aided $7.5 billion in China chip shipments, Information reports
Jensen Huang’s spy scandal may cost Nvidia the China chip fight it was winning
text: Jensen Huang's spy scandal may cost Nvidia the China chip fight it was winning               Jared Blikre      Tue, November 10, 2026 at 5:13 AM MST 3 min read                                NVDA           ^SOX                           Jensen Huang was Washington's loudest voice against cutting China off from American chips, and his spy scandal is now the hawks' best argument. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department hasn't added a single company to its export ban list in 13 months.

The Nvidia (NVDA) CEO admitted Sunday to an affair with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials believe worked for China's Ministry of State Security. Nvidia stock fell about 4% Monday, even as chip stocks (^SOX) jumped nearly 7%. That was Nvidia's worst day during a 5%-plus chip rally since Oct. 28, 1999, months after it went public.

The list in question is Commerce's Entity List. Companies on it need a US license to buy American technology, and those licenses are rarely granted. Commerce added 170 names in 2025 and 366 the year before. It hasn't added one since Oct. 9, 2025, by Yahoo Finance's count.

On Monday, Commerce extended its pause on a rule that would stretch those limits to companies majority-owned by listed firms. But only by two months, to Jan. 10, a week after a new Democratic Congress is sworn in.

"I think Commerce Department is going to batten down the hatches, and they're going to enforce export controls in a way that they weren't doing it before," Isaac Stone Fish, CEO and founder of Strategy Risks, told Deirdre Bosa on Monday.

The tech industry's own leaders see the stakes. "We lead in AI, and that means leading in power. It means leading in compute. It means leading in chips," Bret Taylor, OpenAI's chairman and CEO of AI startup Sierra, told Bosa on the same show. "AI is not particularly popular right now in this country," he added. "So I think this just introduces even more risk."
Huang's case against chip bans was simple. Cut China off, and it builds its own champion.

Huawei is his best exhibit. US sanctions knocked its sales from about $129 billion in 2020 to $95 billion two years later. Last year, it brought in about $123 billion, most of the way back, while building its own AI chips.

Stone Fish points instead to cars, where China absorbed Western know-how and then outbuilt its teachers. "Arguably the best car in the world is not American, Japanese or European, but it's Chinese, and export controls are a way of preventing that from happening," he said.

For Wall Street, it comes down to one person. "If he stays, then this is going to prove to be overdone, and this will be a strong buying opportunity. But if he doesn't stay, it's going to be a problem," Bernstein semiconductor analyst Stacy Rasgon told Bosa. "The only one that wins if he goes probably is China."
Stone Fish disagrees. "This is a net loss for China," he said. "Seeing their dirty laundry aired is a problem for the Communist Party."

items.title: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
text: Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’

China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.

As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.

Green energy is a vital component of the export engine that has kept China’s sluggish post-pandemic economy on track. The success of its exports stands in contrast to its failure to significantly boost domestic general consumption, a structural weakness that has persistently vexed leaders.

In 2025, clean-tech exports surpassed $220bn, and they should grow again this year; the world’s largest emitter is now the world’s leading supplier of clean energy technology. China accounts for about 85% of solar and 80% of lithium-ion battery supply chain production capacity, and in 2025, nearly 75% of electric cars were manufactured there.
Smart moves now by China would position it as a linchpin in a future electrostate world order, persuade rivals to cooperate, and solidify its influence in the global south.

Meanwhile other countries, including the US under Donald Trump, have fallen badly behind. Kerry said they would lose out economically – as well as putting the climate in further danger – unless they, too, embraced low-carbon power and rapid electrification. “The only country that has hugely accelerated is China. The rest of the world is stumbling along while Mother Nature is sending us more powerful signals every week, every day,” he said.

“[China] realised suddenly they had way too much dependency on oil and gas from other places, and they decided they needed to be independent. Other countries, since the war in Iran, and since the strait of Hormuz has been interrupted, have made a similar decision, and they’re moving independently. There’s been a massive uptick in deployment of renewables. Thank you, Donald Trump.”

For autocratic states without free and fair elections, seeing the economic benefits reaped by China would be the spur to adopt low-carbon growth, he added. “They’ll see where the market is going, and they will recognise where the cheaper alternatives are. Even they can read a spreadsheet, and understand where costs are exorbitant [in fossil fuels], and where you have a better deal,” Kerry said. “Right now, renewables together with storage, together with some transitional gas, is cheaper and more effective, than just going with fossil fuels.”

items.title: Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem
text: Following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission on Sunday to an extramarital affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, the chipmaker's relationship to China is about to come under intense scrutiny in Washington, D.C.

Since October 2022, when the Biden administration announced sweeping controls to limit China's ability to obtain advanced U.S. chips, Nvidia has seen its business diminish in the world's second-largest economy. Months after an even stricter set of rules was implemented by the Trump administration, Huang said in October 2025, "We are 100% out of China."

The recent allegations against Huang, while throwing the chipmaker into crisis, have also brought attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China, where its business once flourished. Of particular interest is whether restricted Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies through customers like Singapore-based Megaspeed, the company linked to Alice Huang.

The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring. China has called the allegation a smear.

Jensen Huang has been closely aligned with President Donald Trump during his second administration, helping advise the White House on AI safety regulations, while also pushing for looser restrictions on selling AI chips to China. In December, Trump said Nvidia would be allowed to ship its H200 chips to China, provided the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales. In March, Huang told reporters that Nvidia had "received purchase orders, and we're in the process of restarting our manufacturing."

Huang was a last-minute addition to the roster of tech executives who joined Trump on a trip to China in May, after the White House briefed the president on intelligence concerns, according to the New York Times.
"In 35 years, I haven't seen a chip CEO with this much direct influence on export policy," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO at Moor Insights & Strategy, in an email.

Since last week's midterm elections that included sweeping victories across the country for Democrats, the mood in Washington has changed. Following this weekend's revelations about Huang's affair, three House committees have requested closed-door briefings with the Nvidia CEO about his relationship with Megaspeed.

Democratic lawmakers, who are about to take power in the House and Senate, have said publicly that Congress will investigate and seek answers. Trump said on Monday he was "amazed" by the allegations and that Huang told him he "had no idea that she was a spy." The FBI is now looking into the issue, Trump said at a White House briefing.
It's been a long four years for Nvidia in China.

Prior to the initial export controls in 2022, China made up nearly a quarter of Nvidia's revenue. Nvidia responded to the Biden-era restrictions by redesigning some of its products to comply with the new regulations.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Microsoft presses Trump to scuttle expected ban on Chinese data center technology
How Jensen Huang’s Yearslong Ties to Alice Huang Enabled Nvidia Chip Sales to China
Jensen Huang lobbied ‘very good friend’ Trump for more Nvidia sales to China while ‘caught in Beijing’s honeytrap’
text: SAN FRANCISCO — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made himself President Trump’s “very good friend” and lobbied the administration to loosen restrictions on AI chip sales to China while he was allegedly ensnared in a Chinese honeytrap, a timeline of his reported relationship with Alice Huang shows.

The $150 billion AI boss appeared in loved-up snaps with accused communist spy Alice Huang last year — and then weeks later personally pitched Trump at the White House on relaxing export restrictions for the company’s chips.
Huang missed Trump’s second inauguration, but then more than made up for it with a $25 million donation to the president’s ballroom project.

The 63-year-old appeared at a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025, where he pushed to lift chip restrictions that had just been imposed. There were at least three documented meetings between Trump and Huang where the administration responded with policy changes that made it easier for Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China.
China hawks have long pushed to restrict the most cutting edge chips from the communist regime in an attempt to blunt its technological advances and stymie its attempts to overtake the US on AI.

Huang, for his part, had lobbied and spoken out against restrictions since the Biden administration first imposed limits in 2022. Additionally, selling more chips to the world’s second largest economy could only help Nvidia’s bottom line.

But all the while, Huang — who has been married to college sweetheart Lori for more than 40 years — was meeting with 42-year-old Alice. In May 2025, they were spotted at dinner together during Taiwan’s top tech expo, where she looked at him adoringly and affectionately touched his arm as they sat with other tech honchos.

Alice Huang — a TV host, turned banker, turned executive at the Singapore-based AI computing company Megaspeed — met Jensen Huang (no relation) in early 2024, according to reports. Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars in chips from Nvidia for data centers in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

Separately, the firm — backed by Chinese tech giant Alibaba — is under investigation for allegedly smuggling chips to China. The US government is probing reports that 50,000 chips sold to Megaspeed were seemingly missing following an audit.
Nvidia reportedly intervened in that probe, according to Bloomberg.
The Chinese government denies allegations of a honeypot spy scheme. Megaspeed also denies allegations of wrongdoing.

Trump himself has downplayed Huang’s admission of infidelity and Nvidia’s board said the company, which has no succession plan for replacing Huang, had full confidence in him, even as it announced it was investigating the claims.
On Monday, Trump said he called to check on Huang after he admitted cheating on his wife and apologized to his family.

“I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right,” Trump said at the White House.“He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. I asked him that question. Did you have any idea that she was a spy? He said I had no idea that she was a spy, and I really believe him.”
